raw_response:
I’m farming only 6 mu, so I can’t spread myself too thin. I’ll keep most of the land in the usual wheat-maize rotation because that is the surest way for me to have grain and cash both, and I know that system well. I’ll leave 2 mu for stevia. Stevia can bring better money if the buyer comes on time, but it takes more watching and more hand labor, so I won’t put too much land into it. On the wheat, I’ll do about what worked before: sow in early October, use a local good variety, put most fertilizer as base and add a little more in spring if the leaves look weak. Wheat needs water, so with the well I plan a few irrigations, but not too many because pumping costs money.

After wheat harvest, I’ll rush to plant summer maize right away on the same 4 mu. Around here everybody does it fast, otherwise you lose moisture and the season gets short. I won’t do fancy tillage, just a simple quick field prep and sow. For maize I use hybrid seed because the stand is better and yield is steadier. I’ll give enough fertilizer so it doesn’t go hungry, but I still have to watch cash, so I won’t chase very high rates. Stevia I’ll manage more carefully by hand. That crop can earn more, but if labor is not enough or weather goes wrong, it is troublesome. So this year I stay steady: grain on most land, stevia on a small piece, not too risky.
